data.name: Safecracker: The Ultimate Puzzle Adventure
data.detailed_description:
Como perito em arrombamento de cofres, és contratado pela família abastada de um falecido recente para revistar a sua mansão em busca do seu testamento. Duncan W. Adams era um ávido colecionador de cofres e um "excêntrico", para dizer o mínimo. Adams escondeu a escritura das suas vastas fortunas num de 35 cofres. Tens de os abrir a todos usando pistas espalhadas pela sua mansão extravagante. Os riscos são altos. Usa a tua perícia, astúcia e habilidades de resolução de puzzles para ganhares o teu salário!

  • Um desafiante jogo de aventura e puzzles com 35 cofres únicos para abrir.
  • Muitos puzzles criativos, inteligentes e verdadeiramente únicos.
  • Decifra pistas inesperadas dentro de cada cofre que te ajudarão a abrir os outros, levando-te finalmente ao cofre mestre.
  • Múltiplos níveis de dificuldade para desafiar todos os tipos de entusiastas de puzzles.
  • Explora uma mansão magnífica com 30 divisões luxuosas, intrigantes e detalhadas com precisão.

reviews.review:
[h3]TLDR[/h3]
Safecracker is a short, but sweet puzzle game wherein you try to find the will of a deceased safe enthusiast in his mansion, which is bursting with various puzzles. The game requires some tweaks to work okayish with modern hardware. The rest of its enjoyability depends on your tolerance for puzzles. For 4.99 it's perfectly fine.

[h3]The Good[/h3]
The game is very on point. It knows exactly what it wants to be and delivers: puzzles upon puzzles upon puzzles in a big mansion. There is something for everyone here--clues from pictures/letters you find, sudoku, wordle (with numbers), interlocked switches, chess, ciphers, maths, you name it. I appreciate the inclusion of an in-game map that shows which rooms still have unsolved puzzles and which are done. The music is unintrusive, what little voice-acting there is is fine, and the game features multiple endings, so save before you open the last safe!  Speaking of, there are multiple profiles (keys) and within those multiple safe slots, so multiple people can play this at the same time.

[h3]The Bad[/h3]
It is a very short game. I got tripped up by several of the puzzles to the point where I had to use a walkthrough (I am REALLY awful at combination puzzles and I know diddly-squat about chess), and it still only took me around 5-6 hours to finish. Also, if you are planning to stream it, know that it only works properly in windowed mode and some of the music in there will get your video demonetized. Finally, I am going to save everyone some googling: press S to see UI, left mouse to move/interact, and right mouse to access inventory, map and save menu.

[h3]The Ugly[/h3]
This is a 32 bit game that was very much not designed for modern hardware. To get it running even remotely well, I had to force it into Window mode by editing the bFullScreen= value in the config.ini file in the game's install folder. Once that was done, the game booted in a stable state, but half the UI (including the cursor) was invisible unless I kept S pressed, and sometimes the UI would flicker. Finally, the game crashed when selecting one of the endings (the second time I selected that same ending, it worked).
